validity.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown (currently 405 km, no ref at all). Not one independent source supports anything near 405 km; two independent 2014-15 English trade-press sources on the exact project this row represents (DEKA = Denise-Karawan, operated by Petrobel/Eni/bp) put the real sealine lengths at 9 km (16-in) and 4 km (10-in), tying into an existing 32-in sealine network. 405 km would be roughly the length of the entire Egyptian Mediterranean coastline and is physically implausible for a subsea field tie-in only ~65 km offshore. Almost certainly a transcription artifact: the sheet's own cited 2012 Al-Mal (almalnews) source lists three Denise-project sealines as '3.7 km, 405 km, and 1 km' at 16in/16in/10in -- a lone 3-digit figure sandwiched between two single-digit ones, and no realistic subsea flowline of that length exists in this field. Recommend replacing with a sourced ~4-9 km figure (or marking length as unresolved/uncertain) rather than corroborating 405.
validity.researcher_notes: Chain: (1) GEM's own three refs checked -- petro-news.com/95212 is a generic '39 gas projects in Egypt' listicle; its only relevant passage is about the upstream 'Denise-Karawan field development' (5 wells, $578M) and never mentions a pipeline, length, or diameter. petro-news.com/8215 is a generic Petrobel company-history profile; no mention of Denise, Karawan, or any pipeline. almalnews.com/9021 (Al-Mal, 2012-11-10) is the only ref that actually gives numbers: 'the first [Denise] project includes laying offshore pipelines of length 3.7 km, 405 km, and 1 km, diameters 16in, 16in, and 10in respectively, to carry production from wells to new manifolds... the second project [Karawan] includes an 206 km, 10in offshore pipeline.' Both the 405 km and 206 km figures are outliers next to sub-5km neighbors in the same sentence and read as dropped-decimal artifacts (e.g. 4.05, 20.6). (2) Independent corroboration of the real project (bp/Eni 'DEKA' = Denise-Karawan, first gas Aug 2014): egyptoil-gas.com feature states 'Laying of 4 gas sealines (9 km 16" & 4 km 10") and relevant tie-ins to 32" existing sealine network,' well names Denise North West 1 / Denise North / Karawan / Denise South 6, Seth platform topside tie-in, Denise 70km offshore/~100m depth, Karawan 60km offshore/~68m depth. offshore-energy.biz ('Eni Starts Production from DEKA Project Offshore Egypt') independently corroborates: Temsah Concession, ~65 km north of Port Said, ~100m water depth, gas processed at El Gamil Gas Plant onshore, Denise South 6 first development well, Aug 2014 first gas at 1.8 MMcm/d + ~800 b/d condensate. Two independent modern trade sources agree closely (9km/4km sealines) and neither supports 405 km. (3) GulfPub's Egypt gas roster lists several distinct short Denise-area segments (Akhen-Denise 11km/16in, Denise-Wakar 15km/16in, Denise-Port Said 46km/16in, Denise-El Gamil 41km/16in, Zohr Export I/II to Denise 80km) -- none reaches 100km, let alone 405km, reinforcing that no real single Denise segment is this long. Diameter=16in is plausible/corroborated (matches both the almalnews 16in figure and egyptoil-gas's 9km/16in sealine) -- leaving that value alone.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner/Parent company. Sheet currently lists Owner = Parent company = 'General Petroleum Company (GPC)'. GPC is a distinct, unrelated EGPC-group upstream company (Gulf of Suez fields, e.g. October field) with no stake in Petrobel. Petrobel's actual parents are the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) and Eni (via its Egyptian arm, historically AGIP/IEOC) -- confirmed by the sheet's own cited Operator source. Owner should read EGPC + Eni (or EGPC/IEOC), not GPC.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's own existing Operator ref (petro-news.com/8215, a Petrobel company-history profile, re-verified OK) states Petrobel was 'established under Law 16 of 1978 as an Egyptian joint-stock company between the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation [EGPC] and International Egyptian Oil Company [IEOC/AGIP-Eni's Egyptian subsidiary].' No mention of General Petroleum Company anywhere. Independently, gulfoilandgas.com's Petrobel supplier profile states 'PETROBEL is one of the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation companies jointly owned by ENI' -- a second, independent source agreeing EGPC+Eni, not GPC. Two independent sources agree with each other and both contradict the sheet's current Owner/Parent value.

validity.researcher_notes: The underlying infrastructure is real and operating: this row evidently represents (some segment of) the DEKA -- Denise/Karawan -- subsea gas development in the Temsah Concession, operated by Petrobel (Eni/bp/EGPC), which achieved first gas in August 2014 (Denise South 6 well, ~1.8 MMcm/d + ~800 b/d condensate) per two independent English trade-press sources (offshore-energy.biz, MEED). Fuel=Gas and Operator=Belayim Petroleum Company (Petrobel) are correct and well corroborated. PipelineType=transmission is consistent with GGIT's convention in this roster of cataloging short subsea field-to-shore sealines as transmission (see many other <50km Egypt offshore rows in the same tracker) even though physically this is a subsea gathering/tie-in sealine network rather than a classic long-haul trunk -- not flagging as misclassification since it matches tracker-wide practice. However, the sheet's current Status ref (petro-news.com/95212) is a generic '39 gas projects in Egypt' listicle article that never names 'Denise Gas Pipeline' and does not verify pipeline-specific operating status (url_verifier already flags it: '200 but data value not found'). Recommend swapping to the stronger, pipeline/project-specific refs proposed under fills.

routes.corridor_desc: Independent English trade sources (egyptoil-gas.com, offshore-energy.biz) place the DEKA (Denise-Karawan) subsea wells in the Temsah Concession about 60-70 km offshore in the Eastern Mediterranean / offshore Nile Delta, roughly 65 km north of Port Said in ~68-100 m water depth. Four gas sealines (9 km at 16-in and 4 km at 10-in) tie the subsea wells into Petrobel's existing 32-in sealine network via the Seth platform topside, which in turn runs onshore to the El Gamil Gas Plant near Port Said. No published source gives precise subsea well-head or Seth-platform coordinates, so the offshore end and the intermediate corridor are described only by bearing/distance from Port Said, not a fixed point -- left null rather than guessed. The onshore endpoint coordinate (31.2844, 32.2025) is for the named place 'El Gamil' (fort/airfield landmark, Port Said Governorate) as the nearest sourced fix to the gas plant, not a plant-specific survey point.
routes.researcher_notes: Established end (El Gamil, onshore gas plant) and a loosely bounded offshore origin (Temsah Concession, ~65km N of Port Said) from two independent, verified trade sources. Deliberately left start_lat/start_lon/waypoint coordinates null rather than fabricate a subsea well-head or platform fix that no source actually provides -- suggested_route_accuracy capped at 'low' accordingly, still an improvement over the current 'no route'/blank endpoints.
